title: Chip spec
description: Geometry of one capsule-processor chip. All lengths in millimetres. Origin at the bottom-left corner of the footprint, x to the right, y up the slide, z up out of the slide.

placeholder.description: true while this file holds fake values.

scale.description: Which build envelope in contracts/blocks.json this chip is drawn to. demo (the default, so every existing chip is unchanged): envelope, 30 x 20 mm, and fabrication_floors.max_ports_per_chip (6 ports), which blocks.json states plainly is a DEMO ENVELOPE limit and not a process floor. target: target_envelope, the ANSI/SLAS 127.76 x 85.48 mm microplate footprint, where the port limit lifts and becomes how many ports fit the area at fabrication_floors.min_port_pitch_mm. EVERYTHING ELSE IS IDENTICAL at both scales: one fluidic layer, one etch depth, max_depth_mm 0.3, the in-plane floors (min_open_channel_mm, min_wall_mm, min_port_mm) and the CAD block library. tools/check_chip_spec.py reads this field to pick the envelope and the port rule; a demo chip is checked exactly as strictly as before.

translated_from.description: Optional. Set when this spec was translated by a script from another team member's file in a different format (e.g. chip/modules/module3_step1_3.json). Edit the source, not this file, and re-run the converter. Values the source does not give are marked "placeholder": true where they appear.

module.description: Optional. Which MVP module this chip is. Every part id on a module chip starts with the module prefix (m1_, m1b_, m2_, m3_).

id.description: Module id, also the part-id prefix: m1, m1b, m2, m3.

status.description: draft: parametric draft, not final (the twin shows a 'draft design' badge). superseded: an older design kept for reference; it must not be in a pipeline.

printed.description: true if this chip is fabricated this weekend; false for designed-and-simulated only.

superseded_by.description: For status superseded: the spec that replaced this one, e.g. chip/module1_v1.json.

note.description: Shown next to the status badge, e.g. 'draft – being redesigned by MJ'.

generator.description: Optional. The script that wrote this spec and the parameter values it used (the twin's parameters panel shows them). Regenerate instead of hand-editing.

params_schema.description: JSON Schema of the generator's parameters, e.g. contracts/schemas/generators/m3_wash.schema.json

x.description: Width in mm (75 for a slide).

y.description: Depth in mm (25 for a slide).

layers.description: Material layers listed bottom to top. Each layer starts where the previous one ends; the first starts at z = 0.

run_parameters.description: Optional. Named run parameters this chip accepts (operator/run.py --variant ...). One spec, several instances: e.g. the same Module 1 chip printed twice and run as 'control' and 'interaction'.

valves.description: Optional. On-chip valves. Each sits on a channel and is switched through a control port.

features.description: Optional. Parts that are not chambers, channels or ports: windows, heated zones. They get STLs and twin overlays like any part.

capsule.description: Optional. The capsules this chip is designed for. Checks fall back to contracts/parameters.json when missing.

count.description: Capsules the chip is sized for (capsules, not cells).

trap.description: Optional. Design target for capsule traps.

gap_um.description: Trap gap; must stay below 0.4 x capsule diameter.

capsule_filter.description: Optional. Pre-filter that removes capsule aggregates.

cell_filter.description: Optional. Pillar filter that strains cell clumps before encapsulation.

gap_um.description: Must be <= the encapsulation nozzle width.

nozzle.description: Junction chamber where the droplets form.

core_inlet.description: Port the cells come in through.

stages.description: Optional. Process stages that are not on the chip, between two of its ports (e.g. a cold delay in tubing on a cold block). Commands can target a stage id.

volume_ul.description: [smallest, largest] volume at the design flow.

thermal_zones.description: Optional. Heated or cooled regions, including sub-ambient ones. Checks compare max_temp_c with the chip material's max working temperature.

max_temp_c.description: Hottest set point of the zone. Checked against the chip material's max working temperature (contracts/materials.json).

min_temp_c.description: Optional. Coldest set point. Declare it for any sub-ambient zone (a cold rinse, a -20 C solvent quench), so the zone says what it has to reach and not only what it must survive.

purpose.description: DELIBERATELY A FREE STRING, not an enum: the vocabulary grows with the chemistry, and an enum written today would have excluded module 6's rinse, solvent quench and resolubilisation zones. Values in use: culture, rt, pcr, gelation, rinse, quench, resolubilisation. Only ONE value is load-bearing in code: "culture" (case-insensitive) marks a zone where cells or capsules are grown, and triggers the swollen-capsule chamber-height check in tools/check_chip_spec.py. Everything else is documentation. This matches contracts/README.md, which fixes the field list and the meaning of "culture" and does not close the list of purposes.

note.description: Optional. What this zone is for and why it is at this temperature, e.g. which protocol step drives it.

barcoding.description: Optional. Barcoding scheme. Only PLATE-BASED split-and-pool is dropped; per-CELL barcoding is not. The cell's identity is a RANDOM barcode (random_bases long, so a pool of 4^random_bases) amplified clonally inside that capsule's own oil droplet and overlap-extended onto its cDNA; one capsule holds one cell, so the data IS single-cell. lanes and sublibraries are DEMULTIPLEXING METADATA ONLY (which lineage, which sublibrary) and must NEVER be counted as the barcode space: lanes x sublibraries is about twelve groups, and treating that as the resolution is the arithmetic that made this repo wrongly conclude the assay was lane-level. tools/check_chip_spec.py computes the collision rate over the random pool (4^random_bases) via operator/sizing.py; see contracts/parameters.json barcoding.scheme, barcoding.random_bases and barcoding.loading_mean.

lanes.description: Per-lane barcodes the cells already carry. DEMULTIPLEXING ONLY: not part of the barcode space.

sublibraries.description: Sublibrary indices added by module 4's index PCR. DEMULTIPLEXING ONLY: not part of the barcode space.

random_bases.description: Optional. Length in bases of the RANDOM per-cell barcode, so the barcode space is 4^random_bases (16 bases = about 4.3e9). THIS is what sets the collision rate, and declaring it is what lets the collision rule in tools/check_chip_spec.py fire on this chip. Omit to fall back to contracts/parameters.json barcoding.random_bases.

loading_mean.description: Optional. Mean number of free barcodes loaded per droplet (Poisson). A droplet with none is a lost cell; droplets with several are merged computationally afterwards. Omit to fall back to contracts/parameters.json barcoding.loading_mean.

inferred.description: true where this value was inferred, not taken from the source design (see translated_from).

block.description: Optional. Id of the CAD library block this feature is built from; see contracts/blocks.json. We can only fabricate blocks that exist in that library.

id.description: Join key. STL files are named <id>.stl.

shape.description: box (default): size is [x, y, z]. cylinder: a round chamber, size is [diameter, diameter, depth].

mixer.description: For type mixer: serpentine (a long folded channel, e.g. after a T-junction) or wide_short (a wide, short channel for viscous fluids).

filter.description: For type filter: a pillar (or mesh) filter that particles pass through. Not a capsule trap.

purpose.description: cells: strains cell clumps (gap must be smaller than the encapsulation nozzle). capsule_aggregates: lets single capsules through, stops clumps.

mesh_pore_um.description: Pore size of the mesh floor in micrometres, or null for no mesh.

volume_ul.description: Chamber volume in microlitres (1 mm^3 = 1 uL).

open_top.description: true if the chamber is open to the air at the top, like a well you pipette into. Default false (sealed under a lid).

height_um.description: Optional. Internal height in micrometres, when it differs from size[2] or needs um precision.

sealed.description: Optional. true for a chamber sealed against evaporation (e.g. long incubations).

retention.description: Optional. What holds capsules (or clumps) in the chamber. A WEIR is a standing ridge across the chamber at its outlet that stops short of the lid, so opening_um is the gap left in Z between the crest and the lid. THAT GAP IS A Z DIMENSION AND IS NOT SUBJECT TO THE IN-PLANE FABRICATION FLOOR (contracts/blocks.json fabrication_floors.min_open_channel_mm, 200 um), which limits width only: that is the whole reason a 25 um weir gap is buildable when no printed in-plane gap can retain a 70 um capsule. The crest is relief in the same mould or print, so the chamber is still one fluidic layer at one etch depth. The three optional fields below describe the feature we actually machine (crest_height_um, crest_thickness_um, retains_um), so a weir is fully specified by data instead of by prose in a note.

opening_um.description: Mesh pore, pillar gap or weir gap, in micrometres.

source.description: bought (e.g. a mesh sheet) or fabricated by us (checked against cad/fabrication.json).

crest_height_um.description: Optional, weirs. Height of the standing ridge above the chamber floor in micrometres: the feature a mould or printer actually makes, and the number you would machine from. It is NOT a fixed figure and none is recorded in contracts/blocks.json: DERIVE IT PER CHIP as that chip's etch depth minus opening_um (blocks.json retention.weir_geometry.crest_height_rule), because chips have different depths and a crest taller than its layer cannot exist. So crest_height_um + opening_um is the chamber's depth. This is a Z height, not an in-plane width, so the 200 um in-plane floor does not apply to it.

crest_thickness_um.description: Optional, weirs. Thickness of the ridge along the flow direction, in micrometres. Unlike crest_height_um and opening_um this one IS in plane, so it must be at or above the in-plane fabrication floor (contracts/blocks.json fabrication_floors.min_open_channel_mm, 200 um); blocks.json retention.weir_geometry.crest_thickness_um is exactly that floor.

retains_um.description: Optional. Diameter in micrometres of the SMALLEST particle this retention is meant to hold back, so the opening can be read against what it is for: 70 um for a capsule weir (blocks.json retention.weir_geometry.retains_um), the smallest clump for a cell-clump filter (single cells of 10-20 um pass under the crest on purpose). Larger than opening_um: anything smaller than the opening leaves with the liquid.

block.description: Optional. Id of the CAD library block this feature is built from; see contracts/blocks.json. We can only fabricate blocks that exist in that library.

open_top.description: true if the channel is an open groove with no lid. Default false (closed channel). Flow estimates for open channels are approximate.

capsule_passable.description: Optional, same meaning as ports[].capsule_passable (proposed by MJ). false for a channel deliberately too small to pass capsules or cells, such as a microgroove barrier that passes only soluble factors, vesicles and axons. Such a channel is not checked against capsule diameter.

carries.description: Optional. What flows through it; picks the design rule. capsules / droplets (or unset): width >= 1.5 x capsule diameter. cells: width >= the cell-outlet minimum. liquid / oil / signals: no particle rule.

path.description: Optional. Centreline waypoints [[x, y], ...] in mm, from the 'from' end to the 'to' end. Without it the twin and display model route the channel automatically.

fabricable.description: false for a feature we can't make here (e.g. microgrooves). It is drawn, but not checked against our fabrication limits.

type.description: inlet / outlet for liquid; control for a valve control line.

position.description: Centre of the opening on the chip surface: on top, z = chip height; on the bottom, z = 0.

role.description: Optional. What the port is for.

capsule_passable.description: Optional (Szonja's outlets[].capsule_passable). true if capsules go through this port; false for ports behind a trap, like a waste line below a mesh.

width_um.description: Optional. Opening width in micrometres. Capsule-passable outlets must be >= 1.5 x capsule diameter.

pad.description: Optional PORT PAD: a feature CUT IN THE FLUIDIC LAYER directly under the bore, centred on the port's position, at the fluidic layer's one depth. The bore is drilled through the lid; without a pad every tool clips the port's channels at the edge of the bore's own square, so a 0.8 mm hole opens onto 0 mm2 of channel and lands on solid plastic. With a pad, the port's channels run into the pad and stop on its boundary (cad/make_train_cad.py cuts it: <port_id>_pad.stl and layer PADS in both DXFs), the bore opens onto the pad, and every tool (cad/make_figures.py, tools/check_chip_spec.py, operator/network.py) treats the channel as connected through it. tools/check_chip_spec.py requires the pad to cover the bore, to be wider than each channel that ends on it, and to clear every feature it is not connected to by contracts/blocks.json fabrication_floors.min_wall_mm. Its hydraulic resistance is negligible (a 1.2 mm square 0.3 mm deep) and is not modelled. Opt-in: a port without a pad is exported exactly as before.

shape.description: square: axis-aligned square of side size_mm. round: a circle of diameter size_mm, cut as a regular 64-gon inscribed in it (make_train_cad.PAD_ROUND_SEGMENTS) by every tool alike.

size_mm.description: Side (square) or diameter (round) in mm. At least the bore (width_um, else fabrication_floors.min_port_mm); a round pad must hold the bore's square, so its diameter is at least the bore x sqrt(2) / cos(pi/64).

type.description: State with no control pressure applied.

kind.description: branch: gates a seeding branch. pair: gates the link between two culture chambers (the safety checker blocks opening one in a control run). isolation: anything else.

channel.description: The channel this valve opens or closes.

control_port.description: Port (type control) that switches this valve.

connects.description: For a pair valve: the two chambers it links.
